title: JEP 540 Proposed to Target JDK 28 with a Simple JSON API
gist: JEP 540 moved to Proposed to Target for JDK 28, adding a compact JDK-provided JSON API in an incubating module for parsing, navigating and generating RFC 8259 documents without an external dependency. It is deliberately narrower than Jackson or Gson, excluding data binding and streaming, with a strict parser and immutable value hierarchy that works with pattern matching.

themes.theme: A deliberately minimal built-in JSON API

insights.claim: JEP 540 would add a compact JDK-provided API for parsing, navigating and generating RFC 8259 JSON without an external dependency, shipping in the incubating jdk.incubator.json module where it can change incompatibly or be removed based on feedback.
insights.speaker: A N M Bazlur Rahman
insights.so_what: A standard-library JSON API could reduce reliance on third-party libraries for common config and REST tasks in Java.

insights.claim: The proposal is deliberately narrower than Jackson and Gson, excluding data binding and streaming and offering no permissive parsing mode, instead targeting common tasks like reading a config file, inspecting a REST response, or generating a small JSON payload.
insights.speaker: A N M Bazlur Rahman
insights.so_what: Scoping it narrow leaves object mapping and streaming to the existing ecosystem rather than competing head-on.
insights.locator: The proposal is deliberately narrower paragraph

themes.theme: Design choices: immutability, strictness, pattern matching

insights.claim: The API centers on the Json class and a sealed JsonValue interface permitting six non-sealed subinterfaces for JSON objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans and null, with instances immutable and thread-safe and access methods declared directly on JsonValue so callers traverse without repeated casting.
insights.speaker: A N M Bazlur Rahman
insights.so_what: An immutable sealed hierarchy enables safe traversal and pattern matching, defining the API's ergonomics.
insights.locator: The API centers on the Json class paragraph

insights.claim: The parser provides no lenient mode, rejecting comments, trailing commas and duplicate object-member names even though RFC 8259 only says names should be unique, because differing duplicate-name handling across parsers is an interoperability risk.
insights.speaker: A N M Bazlur Rahman
insights.so_what: Strictness by default trades convenience for predictable, interoperable parsing behavior.
insights.locator: Strictness is another defining choice paragraph

insights.claim: Document construction requires wrapping ordinary Java strings, numbers and booleans in explicit factory methods like JsonString.of and JsonNumber.of, adding ceremony that the author identifies as a likely area for feedback during incubation.
insights.speaker: A N M Bazlur Rahman
insights.so_what: Construction ergonomics are the main trade-off developers will weigh, and may change before the API stabilizes.

insights.claim: JEP 540 succeeds JEP 198, a broader Light-Weight JSON API proposed in 2014 that was never delivered, by concentrating on an immutable in-memory value hierarchy and leaving object mapping, streaming and schema validation to the existing ecosystem, and will require --add-modules jdk.incubator.json on the class path.
insights.speaker: A N M Bazlur Rahman
insights.so_what: A narrower scope than the abandoned 2014 attempt improves the odds this JSON API actually ships.
